purpose: Everolimus is used to treat certain types of cancers, including kidney cancer, breast cancer, and some brain tumors. It is also used to prevent your body from rejecting a transplanted organ, such as a kidney or liver. Your doctor will prescribe it based on your specific condition.
how_it_works: Everolimus works by blocking a specific protein in your body called mTOR, which acts like an 'on switch' for cell growth. By blocking this switch, it slows down or stops cancer cells from growing and dividing. In transplant patients, it calms down the immune system so it does not attack the new organ.
common_side_effects: Mouth sores or ulcers, infections, feeling tired or weak, nausea, diarrhea, swelling in your hands or feet, rash, loss of appetite, and changes in your blood sugar or cholesterol levels.
warnings: This medicine lowers your immune system, so you are more likely to get serious infections — tell your doctor right away if you have a fever or signs of infection. Do not get live vaccines while taking this medicine. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with everolimus. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on why you are taking it. For cancer, it is often one tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food — but always the same way each time. For transplant patients, it is usually taken twice a day. Your doctor will set the exact dose that is right for you and may adjust it over time.
